relevance_note: Case report of one patient with a PSTPIP1 variant: 'Genetic testing revealed a de novo PSTPIP1 gene variant (c.748G>A, p.Glu250Lys)'.
method_note: Hand extraction; a script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Single case report; the parents are included as relatives described in relation to the proband (trio sequencing, unaffected, sex not stated in text, so labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'); they get no variant rows because no variant is attributed to them. Inheritance recorded as de novo from 'Trio whole-genome sequencing revealed a de novo' (trio implies both parents tested; the paper does not separately state each parent negative). Age at onset: the abstract gives 'disease onset at 13 years of age' (matching 'since age 13' for the indurated rashes), but the case text also reports folliculitis-like changes 'for 10 years' at age 16, i.e. earlier; recorded the authors' stated onset of 13 years and the 10-year history as a feature onset. Not recorded as features because the paper gives values without calling them abnormal: CRP 26.39 mg/L, ESR 50 mm/h, hemoglobin 107 g/L, neutrophil count 1.68 × 10^9/L, platelets 199 × 10^9/L, height 170 cm/weight 45 kg; so the checklist items elevated inflammatory markers, anemia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia are 'not reported' (the Discussion's recommendation of IL-1 antagonists 'for better control of symptoms and inflammatory markers' hints that markers were raised but does not state it). Plasma calprotectin and serum zinc were printed with normal ranges and lay inside them; recorded as elevated calprotectin/zinc excluded and the hypercalprotectinemia/hyperzincemia checklist items excluded. Normal gastrointestinal endoscopy and bone marrow are recorded as the paper words them; they do not exclude inflammatory bowel disease (checklist left 'not reported'). 'No superficial lymph node enlargement was palpable' is recorded as a feature but does not exclude the broader lymphadenopathy checklist item. Parents: 'They both denied having a history of skin or joint diseases' was used to exclude the arthritis checklist item (joint disease is broader than arthritis); skin items (pyoderma gangrenosum, acne, etc.) were left 'not reported' for the parents because a denied 'history of skin diseases' was not taken as an explicit statement about acne. Table 1 lists variants per PAID syndrome from Sanz-Cabanillas et al. (2024) without individual-level detail and gives no rows; the Introduction's case counts (87, 15, 6) are literature counts, not individuals. No contradictions found within the paper apart from the onset timing noted above.

treatment_summary.value: topical ointment (no improvement); incision and drainage with anti-infective treatment (no improvement); methylprednisolone 40 mg once daily and cyclosporine 75 mg twice daily (unsatisfactory); methylprednisolone increased to 120 mg per day (improvement); adalimumab 40 mg every 2 weeks with prednisone tapered to 5 mg per day maintenance (PG and abdominal pain relieved, acne not improved); IL-1 antagonists advised
span: He was treated with topical ointment, but no improvement was observed.
Incision and drainage, along with anti-infective treatment, were performed, but no improvement was observed
Methylprednisolone 40 mg once daily and cyclosporine 75 mg twice daily were administered with unsatisfactory results.

Subsequently, adalimumab 40 mg subcutaneously every 2 weeks was given, and the steroid dosage was gradually reduced to prednisone 5 mg per day for maintenance. His symptoms of PG and abdominal pain were relieved, but severe acne did not improve.
The patient was advised to use IL-1 antagonists for better control of the symptoms.
